Run module preservation across many species pairs

Source: R/module_preservation.R
preservation_paired.Rd

Applies module_preservation() to each contrast in pairs. Preservation is directional – whether species A's modules survive in B is a different question from the reverse – so both directions are run and reported separately.

preservation_paired(modules, ...)

# Default S3 method
preservation_paired(
  modules,
  networks,
  orthologs,
  pairs,
  group = NULL,
  edges = NULL,
  cliques = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  z_conserved = 10,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

modules

Named list of detect_modules() results, keyed by species.

...

Additional arguments passed to the default method.

networks

Named list of compute_network() results, keyed by species.

orthologs

Data frame with columns Species1, Species2, hog.

pairs

Data frame with columns sp1, sp2 and optionally pair_name.

group

Optional named vector mapping species to a trait group. When supplied, a group column records "conserved" for preserved modules and the owning species' group for diverged ones. Modules reported "untested" are counted under "untested" rather than a trait group: nothing was measured, so attributing them to one would overstate the evidence.

edges, cliques

Optional find_coexpressologs() and find_cliques() results, used for paralog resolution.

alpha, z_conserved

Passed to classify_preservation().

seed

Integer seed for the whole run, or NULL (default) to draw from the ambient stream and leave it advanced. The seed is applied once here and the per-direction module_preservation() calls are left unseeded, so the directions draw in sequence from one stream instead of every one of them reusing the same permutations. A seeded call restores the caller's stream on exit, the package-wide contract described under detect_modules().

Before 0.3.0 seed reached module_preservation() through ... and handed every direction the identical seed.

Value

A list with classification (one row per module per direction, carrying pair_name, module, species, reference, test, classification and both ordering columns, Zsummary_std and medianRank – the latter ranks within a direction, so it is not comparable across the rows of this table), summary (counts per contrast and direction) and raw (the module_preservation() results, keyed by "<reference>.<test>").

This table feeds tag_permutation() directly: it selects the "diverged" rows and uses reference / test to pick each contrast's two sides.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- preservation_paired(mods, nets, ortho,
  pairs = data.frame(sp1 = "BDIS", sp2 = "BSYL"),
  group = c(BDIS = "annual", BSYL = "perennial")
)
res$summary
} # }
